text:
sanjay: seeing mgmt-plane authz errors in eu-central, console logins 502 and provisioning API 504. Routing controller updates are queuing.

maria: same, console shows 'authz: token validation failed' for a lot of sessions. Started getting support tickets. :grimacing:

liam: config-rollout jobs stuck in leader election loops, leader keeps flapping every ~30s. leader-election timeout in logs.

sanjay: routing-controller prints `RouteUpdateConflict: stale-version` and then backpressure to proxy pools. downstream health probes failing.

ops-bot: Incident created: mgmtplane-authz-storm-1865432100 (priority P1) — paging oncall.

eva: I'm oncall, joining. Any immediate mitigation we can do for console/provisioning?

maria: thinking traffic shift off eu-central. What's spare capacity in na-west2/dedicated pools?

liam: dedicated pools: na-west2 has ~20% spare GPU headroom if we evict low-priority jobs. na-east1 ~10%.

sanjay: workaround attempt: increase auth-proxy replicas in eu-central by +3. Trying `kubectl scale deploy/auth-proxy -n mgmt --replicas=6` but API returns 503 from mgmt API.

maria: if we can't scale control-plane components, do manual local proxy sidecars on app nodes? I can push a DaemonSet with local auth cache to reduce RTT.

maria: pushed temporary sidecar DS: `kubectl apply -f tmp/auth-proxy-sidecar-daemon.yaml` — sidecars up on ~60% nodes, auth errors dropped for those nodes.

liam: provisioning backlog growing: job scheduler shows `validate_api_token` failing for new node leases. GPUs queued at length 320. Evicting batch jobs with lowest priority to free 8 GPUs.

deploy-bot: starting traffic-shift playbook (runbook 9.2): step 1 lock rollouts, step 2 set route-weights, step 3 monitor error rates.

maria: locking rollouts now (`mgmtctl rollout lock --scope=global`) — command succeeded.

sanjay: initiating route weight change: shifting 60% traffic from eu-central -> na-west2, 30% -> na-east1, 10% remain eu-central. `mgmtctl traffic-shift --from=eu-central --to=na-west2=0.6,na-east1=0.3 --duration=5m`

deploy-bot: traffic-shift executed; stepping weights over 5m. Monitoring: 1m checks at 30s intervals.

eva: observed 40% reduction in auth failures after 90s on shifted services. Console still flaky for some SSO sessions.

liam: found root cause signal: a recent config push to authz introduced cache key cardinality spike — cache eviction thrash + rate-limit hits on KMS calls. KMS itself fine, but auth layer overwhelmed.

maria: can we rollback that config? It was `authz/cache-policy:v2026-03-14`.

sanjay: initiating rollback of last config commit. `gitops rollback authz/cache-policy v2026-03-13` -> apply.

ops-bot: Rollback start acknowledged by CI.

liam: rollback finished at +18m, auth proxy logs show cache hit rate stabilizing. KMS calls reduced.

maria: manual console workaround: support org can use temporary SSO bypass tokens issued by `support-token-service` until session cleanup completes. Issued ~100 tokens so far.

sanjay: started incremental restart of routing-controller to clear queued updates. Performed restart on 3 replicas; leader stabilized.

maria: provisioning errors dropping, GPU queue down to ~40. Evicted jobs rescheduled into na-west2.

eva: traffic-shift completed: final weights = na-west2 0.6, na-east1 0.3, eu-central 0.1. No major error spikes during step-down.

liam: post-fix checks: auth error rate back to baseline after ~22 minutes. Config rollout lock still in place.

sanjay: console access restored for most users, provisioning APIs returning 200. Monitoring for 30m before full rollback of traffic.

maria: opening follow-up ticket: INFRA-3374 — root cause analysis + permanent mitigations (cache-size sanity, rate-limit backoff, rollout guard).

eva: good job team. We'll keep the ticket and schedule a blameless postmortem. closing incident in 1h after observation window. :thumbsup:

sanjay: closing notes: avoid large cardinality cache keys in authz policies; add rollout preflight that simulates cache effects.

maria: adding datasheet + KB entry for support bypass procedure.

ops-bot: Incident resolved (P1 -> resolved). Follow-up: INFRA-3374 created.

sanjay: thanks everyone.
